item.title: A ball, A god, and A biological something: A ball, A god, and A biological something

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Thanks for getting back to me.

I think I overused the word “exact” in my description here, it should say “similar.” The events are not exactly the same, and it leaves room for a couple of interpretations of what the anomaly actually IS. The second foundation is introduced early on, what I’m going for is for the reader to debate with themselves throughout the article or at the end with whether the PCS Foundation is anomalous, if they’re non-anomalous and have been abusing anomalies to avoid detection, or if NONE of it is anomalous. The SCP Foundation themselves will be having this debate alongside the reader, the addendum will be riddled with Staff Surveys (that the reader can also take) to attempt to get a general consensus on what they believe the PCS foundation to be/be doing so that they can work with certainties, and at the end, our three theories will be proposed in three separate theory documents.

item.title: Looking for greenlight: Looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): None

Page Layout (Optional): A normal SCP article with a long description short addendum and clear containment procedures.

Elevator Pitch: An infection caused by a fictional strain of hummingbirds.

Central Narrative: A microscopic hummingbird egg instance that infects a person and has three very deadly stages that include taking over the person's throat. cutting the vocal cords and veins in the neck. Then damaging the core parts of the brain then killing the infected person. Then breaking the person's jaw and flying out. Then laying new eggs. The eggs stay airborne for 30 days. The stages last over 4-6 months and it is classified as a Keter SCP. Here is the draft http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/sogn67893

item.title: Scp idea: Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
Moved to Ideas Critique since there's no draft here.

Also noting that this:

An scp that knows everything there is know about the foundation, it's object class is: Thaumiel so it must be helpful? Well yes (sometimes) but mostly no, it hates almost everyone in foundation

Doesn't make sense for a Thaumiel anomaly. If it's not a reliable form of containment, it shouldn't be Thaumiel. Doesn't matter how overpowered and intelligent it is; if the Foundation can't trust it, they won't use it. Moving forward, I suggest reading over this essay on common SCP pitfalls to get an idea of what elements to avoid putting in an SCP article.
